title: Improved heritability partitioning and enrichment analyses using summary statistics with graphREML.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Fetched the Zenodo landing page for record 15085817 ('Data release for graphREML', CC-BY 4.0, open). It lists four tarballs: sumstats20traits.tgz, precision_ukbb.tgz, scores20traits.baselineld.tgz and baselineld.tgz. File sizes shown were 416.1 MB, 917.1 MB, 1.8 GB and 6.9 GB (about 10.0 GB in total); I could not reliably match each size to its file name. The Zenodo API timed out. Code is on GitHub (huilisabrina/graphREML, oclb/graphld). I did not download or open any tarball.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything about the method and results comes from the abstract and the Zenodo description, because there is no PMCID and no open full text. That includes: likelihood-based heritability partitioning on GWAS (genome-wide association study) summary statistics using LDGMs (sparse linkage-disequilibrium graphical models), 2.5x more significant enrichments than S-LDSC (stratified LD score regression), 20 UK Biobank traits, and baselineLD annotations.

a1_downloadable.note: Zenodo record is open (CC-BY 4.0). The landing page lists the files, but I did not download them.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: No measured outcome column. The outputs are heritability enrichments and per-SNP (single-nucleotide polymorphism) heritabilities, which graphREML or S-LDSC must estimate from summary statistics plus LD matrices. Any label would have to be built by running a statistical model. Judged from the Zenodo description, not the files.

a3_inputs_present.note: Zenodo says baselineLD annotations and per-SNP summary statistics are included. Not opened.

a4_units_stated.note: Standard GWAS formats (z-scores, sample sizes). Not checked in the files.

a5_enough_rows.note: Millions of SNPs per trait, but only 20 traits; the trait is the real unit for enrichment questions. I did not count rows.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: about 10 GB compressed for all files; the annotation tarball alone is about 1.8 to 6.9 GB
a6_fits_laptop.note: The full release is over the 5 GB working-set threshold. Subsetting is possible but still heavy.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Not checkable without full text; Zenodo states 20 traits.

a8_label_provenance.note: Any 'label' (per-SNP heritability, enrichment) is the output of graphREML or S-LDSC, computed from the same annotations that would be the features. Training on it would mean distilling a statistical model, with circularity built in.

existing_models.name: graphREML (this paper; code at huilisabrina/graphREML and oclb/graphld)
existing_models.score_and_split: Per the abstract, 2.5x more significant trait-annotation enrichments than S-LDSC, with concordant estimates, in simulations and real traits. No ML-style split applies.

existing_models.name: S-LDSC (stratified LD score regression)
existing_models.score_and_split: The comparator in this paper; described in the abstract as lower power. No split.

backbone.name: None fits directly; sequence models such as AlphaGenome could supply SNP annotations, but not as freeze-and-head on this data
backbone.hardware: CPU, but a working set of 10 GB or more
backbone.licence: Data CC-BY 4.0; UK Biobank-derived summary statistics are public

honest_claim_h3: Any model trained here would only reproduce graphREML's own estimates of per-SNP heritability from annotations, not a measured biological quantity.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use functional annotations of each DNA variant to predict how much that variant contributes to the heritability of a trait.
plain_idea.train_on: Per-variant functional annotations (baselineLD) plus GWAS summary statistics for 20 UK Biobank traits; row count unknown (files not opened).
plain_idea.predict: Per-variant heritability or annotation enrichment. There is no direct measurement: the 'truth' is itself estimated by graphREML or S-LDSC from the same annotations.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Statistical geneticists want to know which genome functions carry trait heritability, but graphREML already answers this directly. An ML layer would add circularity, not information.

more_or_better_data.why: We would have the same 20 UK Biobank traits that graphREML was run on; there is no extra data.

confidence_score.why: graphREML is likelihood-based and already reports standard errors and calibrated per-SNP heritability estimates, per the abstract.

models_beatable.why: graphREML (2026) is a likelihood method published in Nature Genetics; there is no ML benchmark or split to beat.

guaranteed_improvement.why: There is no measured label, so no new joinable data could measure the same quantity in the same way.

ml_idea: Considered: predict per-SNP heritability or enrichment from annotations or sequence embeddings. Rejected because the target is a statistical estimate computed from those same annotations.

effort.compute_note: Working set taken from the Zenodo file sizes (about 10 GB total); no timing done.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Ask whether any column in the release is a measurement rather than a model estimate. From the Zenodo description, none is.

verdict_reason: Statistical-genetics method paper with no measured label: heritability enrichments and per-SNP heritabilities are graphREML or S-LDSC estimates computed from the same annotations (A2 and A8 fail), and the release is about 10 GB (A6).
